overview: A minimal single-page web application serving a static 'Hello World' message. The architecture consists of a single frontend component that delivers HTML content directly to visitors without requiring backend API dependencies. The web application is containerized and deployed as a standalone service.
requirements: The application must display 'Hello World' text when accessed
The application must be accessible via standard web browsers
The application must respond immediately on page load
The application must include a health check endpoint for monitoring
The application must be containerized using Docker
The application must run as a Kubernetes deployment

components.name: hello-world-web
components.openAPISpec:
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Hello World Web Application
  version: 1.0.0
  description: A simple web application that displays Hello World
paths:
  /health:
    get:
      summary: Health check endpoint
      description: Returns the health status of the web application
      operationId: healthCheck
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Application is healthy
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  status:
                    type: string
                    example: ok
                  timestamp:
                    type: string
                    format: date-time
                    example: '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z'
components.componentAgentInstructions: Implement a React-based single-page application using TypeScript and Vite as the build tool. Create a minimal React component that renders 'Hello World' as the main heading (h1 element). The application should use React 18+ with functional components. Configure Vite to build the application for production with optimized assets. The Docker container should use a multi-stage build: first stage uses node:18-alpine to build the React app with 'npm run build', second stage uses nginx:alpine to serve the static files. Copy the built files from /dist to /usr/share/nginx/html. Create a custom nginx.conf that serves the app on port 8080 (not 80) and includes a /health endpoint that returns JSON {status: ok, timestamp: current ISO timestamp} with 200 status. The nginx config should support client-side routing by redirecting all non-file requests to index.html. Include proper CORS headers if needed. The package.json should include react, react-dom, typescript, vite, and @vitejs/plugin-react. The health endpoint must return valid JSON and should not depend on the React application state. Ensure the Docker EXPOSE directive specifies port 8080. The application should have a clean, centered layout with the Hello World text prominently displayed. Include a basic CSS reset and minimal styling to ensure cross-browser compatibility. The build should produce optimized, minified production assets.
